planting.note: Start seed indoors 10 weeks before the last frost and transplant out once soil has warmed, keeping the bed evenly moist throughout the season.

directions: Ventura is a vigorous, disease-resistant green stalk celery bred for reliable performance in home gardens and market rows alike, producing thick, crisp, well-filled ribs without the fussiness of older heirloom types. Its heat tolerance and slow-to-bolt habit make it more forgiving than many stalk celeries during warm spells, and it needs no blanching to stay pale and mild. Feed heavily and keep the root zone consistently moist, since any drought stress produces stringy, hollow stalks. Gardeners choose Ventura when they want a dependable, all-purpose green celery that performs well from spring through fall without special handling.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 10 weeks before the last frost and transplant into rich, moisture-retentive soil after danger of frost passes.

directions: Giant Red is a 19th-century English heirloom celery valued for its tough, deep pink-to-red stalks and pronounced, old-fashioned celery flavor that is stronger and more concentrated than modern green types. Traditionally grown in trenches and earthed up to blanch and sweeten the ribs, it can also be left unblanched for a more intense, almost peppery flavor better suited to cooked dishes than raw eating. It tolerates cool fall weather better than many stalk celeries, holding quality after light frost. Gardeners grow it for its striking color in soups and braises and as a genetic link to celery grown before uniform green hybrids became standard.

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost, or start a fall crop in mid to late summer since Orion resists bolting better in longer days than older Florence types.

directions: Orion is a hybrid Florence fennel selected for improved bolt resistance and uniform, rounded bulb formation, making it more reliable than open-pollinated types for both spring and fall sowings. Bulbs develop a tight, flattened-round shape with tender, sweetly anise-flavored flesh and stay in good condition in the field longer than older cultivars before splitting or flowering. Give it consistent moisture and full sun to encourage smooth, well-formed bulbs, and harvest promptly once bulbs reach baseball to tennis-ball size. Gardeners who have struggled with fennel bolting in variable spring weather choose Orion for its dependability across a wider sowing window.

planting.note: Direct sow in spring after frost danger passes, or sow again in mid-summer for a fall bulb crop in cooler weather.

directions: Preludio is an early-maturing hybrid Florence fennel bred to size up quickly into smooth, glossy white bulbs while resisting the premature bolting that plagues fennel sown in lengthening spring days. Its speed makes it a favorite for the first fennel planting of the season, when growers want a harvestable bulb well before summer heat sets in. The flesh is crisp and mildly sweet with the characteristic anise flavor, equally good raw in salads or roasted. Choose Preludio specifically for early-season plantings where bolt resistance and a short days-to-maturity window matter most.

planting.note: Soak seed overnight and direct sow or transplant after last frost; parsley germinates slowly so keep the seedbed consistently moist.

directions: Forest Green is a tightly curled parsley selected for its dark, glossy foliage and dense, upright habit that holds its color and vigor later into the season than older curly strains. The deeply ruffled leaves are excellent for garnish work while still offering good fresh-eating flavor, milder than flat-leaf types. It performs well in containers and edging plantings thanks to its compact, uniform growth. Gardeners pick Forest Green when they want a curly parsley with richer color and better heat tolerance than standard moss-curled selections.

planting.note: Direct sow into loose, deeply worked soil once it is workable in spring, since roots fork in heavy or rocky ground.

directions: Andovy is a Hamburg-type root parsley grown for its smooth, parsnip-like white taproot rather than its foliage, with a mild, earthy, parsley-scented flavor that works well roasted, mashed, or added to stocks. It produces uniform, straight, slow-to-fork roots when grown in loose soil, along with edible flat leaves that can be harvested lightly through the season without harming root development. As a hardy biennial root, it can be left in the ground and harvested through fall and into early winter after light frosts, which sweetens the flavor. Gardeners grow Andovy as a dual-purpose crop, choosing it over standard leaf parsley when a storable root vegetable is the goal.
